historical_references.reference: Akeeq ibn As-Salt, a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), is reported to have given the first sermon (khutbah) after the conquest of Mecca in 630 CE. He was born in the tribe of Qais Ibn Hailan, and was known for his piety and generosity. He was appointed as the governor of Mecca after the conquest and played a significant role in the early Islamic history.
historical_references.context: First sermon after the conquest of Mecca, Appointed as the governor of Mecca

historical_references.reference: Akeeq ibn Abdulkarim, a prominent figure in the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 CE), was a vizier (advisor) to several caliphs, including Harun al-Rashid and Al-Ma'mun. He was known for his wisdom, integrity, and patronage of learning and the arts. He played an instrumental role in the expansion of the Abbasid Caliphate and the development of the Islamic Golden Age.
historical_references.context: Vizier to several Abbasid Caliphs, Patron of learning and the arts, Instrumental role in expanding the Abbasid Caliphate
